Summary — 2026-10-17 @ 4781c64 (full review, 11 aspects, scope: whole repo)

Worst aspect(s): Logic correctness (LOG) and Requirements alignment (REQ) at 0/10. Open criticals:

  • LOG-001 C: reschedule never checks the booking's original start, so R27 and the R6 window can be bypassed.
  • LOG-002 C: rescheduling a HELD booking renews its hold deadline.
  • LOG-003 C: the outbox claim publishes event N+1 while N is in backoff.
  • LOG-004 C: ending a rule with no body uses the UTC date, not the provider's local date.
  • LOG-005 C: reschedule silently drops resourceRef.
  • ERR-001 C: a broker outage starves the hold-expiry and auto-complete sweeps (one scheduler thread).
  • SEC-001 C: the internal contacts endpoint serves any booking's PII to any token holder.
  • SEC-002 C: POST /v1/providers makes any token holder a provider admin (owner declined the hazard).
  • CON-001 C: an availability edit racing a create stores a booking inside blocked time and leaves it off the R20 conflict list.
  • REQ-001 C: a provider can cancel without the reason R7 requires.
  • REQ-002 C: no metric or alert exists for undispatched events (NF11).
  • REQ-003 C: BookingCompleted does not say whether the system or the provider completed it (UC12).
  • REQ-004 C: there is no erasure, export or retention (NF5).

First review of this repository (no prior ledger): 83 findings recorded. Of these, 48 are critical or major. 39 of those passed a clean-context verifier: none was refuted, and one fact correction moved CON-001 to critical. The other 9 are TSQ majors, each confirmed by a green mutation run.

Declared assumptions (scout pass @ 4781c64, 2026-10-17)

Evidence-based detections; each states the weakest claim its evidence supports. Override any of these in User overrides — overrides persist and bind future reviews.

  • Language(s): Kotlin 2.3 (about 3.2k lines in main, 1.5k in test) and PostgreSQL SQL/plpgsql (ddl about 1.2k lines, plus 33 statement files). One Gradle module.
  • House pattern standard: Kotlin, repo-declared (README "Layout", data-design.md §4). It has these parts:

- core/ holds domain types, pure rules and ports, with no framework imports (verified). - repo/ holds JdbcClient adapters that load SQL from resources. - api/ holds controllers that delegate to core. - sys/ holds wiring; worker/ holds Kafka and the schedules. - Every multi-statement write is one plpgsql call. - There is no ORM, and tests use hand-written fakes. - No linter or formatter is configured.

  • Auth model: in-code. A JWT resource server with a required issuer; every path except /actuator/** needs a token, /internal/** included (sys/SecurityConfig.kt:22-29). Authorization comes from provider_admin membership in the database. No network isolation is committed: "never routed through public ingress" (InternalController.kt:13) is a comment only. Any holder of an issuer token is an untrusted caller (domain-context §5).
  • Deployment model: assumed, never deployed. Basis: owner statement in domain-context §4; there are no manifests.

- Designed topology: at least 2 booking-api and at least 2 booking-worker replicas from one image, chosen by profile. The relay and both sweeps run on every worker. - Design targets, never measured: about 500 providers, 2,000 resources, 10k bookings/day, 50 req/s search and 10 req/s writes. - Hikari pool of 10. The relay runs every 500 ms in batches of 100; the expiry sweep every 30 s; auto-complete hourly.

  • Consumed contract surfaces: none have a consumer.

- The HTTP /v1/** API is undeployed. - booking-lifecycle-v1 is an unpublished draft (owner). - booking-gate-resolution-v1 has no producer. - The schema reaches the database through Flyway at every pod startup, from migrations generated out of ddl/ (build.gradle.kts:64-80).

  • Tests: JUnit 5, in three tiers: pure unit tests, hand-faked orchestration tests, and *IT tests against real PostgreSQL (Testcontainers, or BOOKING_TEST_JDBC_URL).

- The command ./gradlew test --offline works here. - Baseline @4781c64: 72 tests, 5 failing. ApplicationContextIT fails 3 times (TSQ-009) and the BookingLifecycleIT relay pair fails twice (TSQ-001).

  • Exclusions:

- build/, .idea/ and the Gradle wrapper - the documentation tooling: docs/backend-design/build-review.mjs, package*.json and design-review.html (owner: not a module) - the generated data-dictionary.yaml

  • Domain facts: from domain-context §4 and §7, owner-confirmed.

- No money anywhere. Durations are in minutes; horizon and grace in days. One booking takes one unit of capacity. - Instants are UTC; rules are wall-clock times in the provider's IANA zone. The session's values are authoritative over the current service row. - HELD and CONFIRMED hold capacity; the other five states are terminal. - Domain rejections are BK001–BK009; any other SQLSTATE is a defect. - Create is idempotent on (customer, key). - The outbox is at-least-once: the claim takes no lock and consumers dedupe on eventId. - The gate consumer dedupes on inbox_message.message_id. Events carry identifiers only.

  • Sweeps run (src/main + ddl unless noted):

- Raw identifier splices: SQL keyword next to ${, $x or "+, or EXECUTE. 1 hit (ddl/01:341, a trigger EXECUTE FUNCTION); suppressed. All SQL is resource files with bound params. - Failure collapsed to a benign value: catch (, runCatching, ?: emptyList(), EXCEPTION WHEN. 5 hits: RuleViolations.kt:16 (translation), OutboxRelay.kt:33 (row retained; feeds REQ-002 and LGG-001), ListingService.kt:27 (correct for UC10), ddl/03:348 and :595 (re-raise as BK001). No collapse finding. - Init-only schema delivery: initdb, init.sql, flyway. 0 init-only hits; Flyway runs at startup. The delivery question leads to CMP-001. - Ungated tests touching real systems (src/test): DataSource, JdbcClient, PostgreSQLContainer. 5 files plus ApplicationContextIT, all gated by Testcontainers or an env var. The unguarded clean() is TSQ-010. - Silently-defaulting selectors: X? = null, ?:, orElse, plpgsql DEFAULT. 25+ hits. Leads: BookingDtos.kt:45 (LOG-005), AvailabilityAdminController.kt:66 (LOG-004, LOG-009, PAT-003), ddl/03:88 (CMP-002). The rest are suppressed (deliberate PD14 selection, membership-bound on-behalf, owner-confirmed contact fill). - Secrets adjacent to logging: 26 log calls. No credential or customer PII on a reachable path. ApiExceptionHandler.kt:41 renders pgjdbc row detail (LGG-003). - Discarded external-mutation results: send().get, dropped .update(). 6 hits. JdbcProviderSetupRepository.kt:77 leads to LOG-010; :43 folds into ERR-003; the rest are guarded in SQL. - Numeric parse collapsed to zero: toXOrNull, toInt(), parseInt. 0 hits. - Retry budget against the caller's deadline: - Kafka .get(10 s) with max.block.ms left at 60 s, 100 events per pass, all on one shared scheduler thread. This is ERR-001. - Producer retries after the 10 s timeout cause duplicate publishes, which is credited (at-least-once). - The backoff is capped at 5 min with unlimited attempts. - Caller-supplied clock or identity: request startsAt, resourceRef, onBehalfOfCustomerRef, contact fields, linkedSubject. startsAt is checked against the server clock; linkedSubject leads to SEC-007 (latent); the rest are suppressed. No request field names "now".

  • Domain-context checklist:

- I1 (one occupied session per resource): held — ddl/01-create-tables.sql:300-302. The concurrency probe found 0 overlaps in 11.8k creates. - I2 (capacity per session): held — ddl/03-functions.sql:342-345, 589-592, CHECK at ddl/01:296. - I3 (one event per committed transition): held — ddl/01:445, ddl/03:421, 510-511. - I4 (no PII in events): held — ddl/03:171-212 is the only outbox writer. - I5 (absent, not forbidden): violated at api/InternalController.kt:27-29 (SEC-001). - I6 (transitions are rows): held — ddl/03:437-445. - Hazard, POST /v1/providers self-service: owner declined, filed as SEC-002. - Hazard, gate consumer with no dead-letter: owner declined, filed as ERR-005 (latent). - Not exercised: the internal contacts endpoint has no legitimate caller (SEC-001 reach rests on an untrusted caller); resource.idp_subject is read by nothing (REQ-010, SEC-007); the reschedule resource-change plumbing is unused, but the dropped field sits on the exercised reschedule (LOG-005); nothing crosses the Kafka edges (ERR-004/005/006, SEC-008, TYP-001 latent); AWAITING_PAYMENT is unreachable.

  • External-state journeys: 11 operations enumerated.

- Operations: create (including replay), cancel, approve, decline, attendance, reschedule, the expiry sweep, the auto-complete sweep, gate consume, relay publish/mark/record, provider setup writes, and availability rule and exception writes. - Empty or problematic cells: - create, ambiguous: concurrent same-key requests → CON-004. - create, replay with a different body → LOG-011. - sweeps, delayed: starved by the relay → ERR-001. - relay, partial order: → LOG-003. - relay, rejected by the broker, persistently: no escalation → REQ-002. - gate consume, partial: claim before effect → ERR-004. - gate consume, malformed: → ERR-005. - gate consume, unknown booking: → ERR-006. - provider setup, partial: → ERR-003. - provider setup, already-linked: → LOG-010. - setup and availability writes, pre-flight CHECK: → ERR-002. - setup and availability writes, retries: → ERR-007. - availability edit vs create: → CON-001. - Every other cell is decided or credited.

  • Scoring interpretation: none → 10; minors only → 9 flat (listed and counted, never deducted); within the worst open C/M tier each verified finding counts one unit (widespread majors count two; doubling never applies to criticals); score = band start − step × (units − 1), clamped at the band floor (critical 3/−1/0, major 6/−1/4). The first unit is free — it sets the band: a single widespread major is 2 units → 6 − 1×1 = 5, never 4. Unverified C/M claims are listed as candidates and do not count.

Logic correctness (LOG) — 0/10 · 13 open

LOG-001 · C · isolated — Reschedule never checks the original start, so R27 (and the R6 window) can be bypassed

  • docs/backend-design/ddl/03-functions.sql:558-564 (only a terminal check), :614-630 (row rewritten, then fn_transition_booking re-reads the new start), :464-481; permitting rules at 04-seed-lookups.sql:57-59
  • Worksheet: reach customer or provider holding a CONFIRMED booking, via POST /v1/bookings/{ref}/reschedule · residue external · signal none → critical
  • Intent: R27 ("After start, the only remaining transitions are the attendance ones"), and the comment at :470. Failing input (probe): a booking for 11-02 10:00Z, rescheduled at 11-02 12:00Z to 11-09, stays CONFIRMED and moves. A booking inside the window: direct cancel → BK007; reschedule out of the window → succeeds; cancel → succeeds.
  • Cross-ref: REQ (R27, UC8).

LOG-002 · C · isolated — Rescheduling a HELD booking renews its hold deadline

  • ddl/03-functions.sql:603-620; core/booking/GatePolicy.kt:27-34
  • Worksheet: reach customer at an approval-mode provider · residue external (capacity held past the gate TTL, renewable until start; PD5 sets no reschedule limit) · signal none → critical
  • Intent: requirements §4.1, HELD→HELD: "new time only, hold reason and deadline unchanged". Failing input: a hold created 11-01 08:00Z has deadline 11-02 08:00Z; a reschedule at 11-02 07:59Z moves the deadline to 11-03 07:59Z.
  • Cross-ref: REQ.

LOG-003 · C · isolated — Outbox claim applies backoff before picking each booking's oldest event, so N+1 is published while N waits

  • src/main/resources/sql/outbox/claim_due_events.sql:24-30; record_failure.sql:5; core/outbox/OutboxRelay.kt:39-44
  • Worksheet: reach relay on every worker; any failed or timed-out send of N while N+1 exists (e.g. broker recovery) · residue external (booking-lifecycle-v1 permanently carries N+1 ahead of N for that key) · signal none → critical
  • Intent: the file's own comment ("event N+1 … is never sent while N is still unsent"), R29, domain-context §7. The probe claim returned only seq 2 while seq 1 was in backoff. The draft-topic status lowers the cost of a fix, not the reach. Domain-context §7's "only the oldest undispatched event per booking is claimed" is contradicted by this code.
  • Cross-ref: CON, TSQ-002.

LOG-004 · C · isolated — Ending a rule with no body sets effective_until to today's UTC date, not the provider's local date

  • api/AvailabilityAdminController.kt:66; ddl/03-functions.sql:54-61
  • Worksheet: reach provider admin ending a rule with no body while the provider-local date differs from UTC · residue external (rule persisted one day long or short) · signal none → critical
  • Intent: R14. Failing input: an America/Los_Angeles provider ends a rule at 2026-10-17 18:00 PDT. The stored date is 2026-10-18, so local Oct 18 still offers 29 slots. Pacific/Auckland loses today early.
  • Cross-ref: PAT-003, LOG-009.

LOG-005 · C · isolated — Reschedule accepts resourceRef on the wire and silently drops it

  • api/BookingDtos.kt:45; api/BookingController.kt:88 (newResourceId = null); ddl/03-functions.sql:569 (COALESCE to the old resource); dead plumbing at BookingLifecycleService.kt:72,79, JdbcBookingLifecycle.kt:73
  • Worksheet: reach any caller sending resourceRef on the exercised reschedule operation · residue external (booking moved to the new time on the old resource; event emitted) · signal none (TransitionResponse carries no resource) → critical
  • Failing input: {startsAt:T, resourceRef:R2} for a booking on R1 → booking on R1@T, 200. Verifier: the domain-context not-exercised entry describes this defect's own mechanism, so the path is not latent.
  • Cross-ref: CMP, REQ (UC8), RDB (dead plumbing).

LOG-006 · M · isolated — Availability search applies neither R4 lead time nor R5 horizon and offers past starts

  • ddl/03-functions.sql:84-156 (comment :156 "R4 and R5 are applied by the caller"); core/availability/AvailabilityService.kt:22-27; sql/availability/search_availability.sql:1-2
  • Worksheet: reach any caller · residue request · signal none → major
  • Intent: UC4. A search over a past date returns 29 slots; so does one beyond the 90-day horizon; creating any of them yields BK004/BK005.
  • Cross-ref: REQ (UC4).

LOG-007 · M · isolated — Slot grid anchored to the query's from, not the window start

  • ddl/03-functions.sql:75-78, :128, :138
  • Worksheet: reach any search whose from falls inside a window (from=now, a paginated page 2) · residue request · signal none → major
  • Intent: data-design OQ2. With from=09:07 the offered starts are 09:07 and 09:22, and an existing 09:15 session with room never matches (exact starts_at join), so it vanishes from results.

LOG-008 · M · isolated — A customer cannot withdraw a HELD request inside the cancellation window

  • ddl/03-functions.sql:473-480
  • Worksheet: reach customer at an approval-mode provider whose start is within 24 h · residue request (BK007; the hold persists) · signal caller → major
  • Intent: UC6, and requirements §4.1, where HELD→CANCELLED needs only "Before start time" (R6 sits on the CONFIRMED row).
  • Cross-ref: REQ.

LOG-009 · M · isolated — A rule with a future effective_from cannot be ended; the attempt returns 500

  • api/AvailabilityAdminController.kt:66; sql/management/end_availability_rule.sql:3-9; CHECK availability_rule_dates_forward at ddl/01-create-tables.sql:239
  • Worksheet: reach provider withdrawing a pre-published rule · residue request · signal caller (500) → major
  • Evidence: the default "today" is before effective_from, giving 23514 → 500. Even an explicit date leaves at least one day published.

LOG-010 · M · isolated — Re-linking an already-linked service and resource answers 404 "no such provider, service or resource"

  • sql/management/link_service_resource.sql:10; repo/JdbcProviderSetupRepository.kt:77; core/management/ProviderSetup.kt:89-93; api/ProviderSetupController.kt:106-110
  • Worksheet: reach any admin retrying the link (e.g. after a lost 204) · residue request · signal caller (misleading) → major
  • Evidence: two identical POSTs give 204 then 404, although the link exists.

LOG-011 · M · isolated — Idempotency replay ignores the request body

  • ddl/03-functions.sql:315-325; api/BookingOutcomeResponder.kt:25-35
  • Worksheet: reach any client reusing a key · residue request · signal none → major
  • Evidence: key K for slot T1, then POST {startsAt:T2} with K → 200 with booking A(T1). No booking exists at T2, and the body does not show the mismatch.
  • Cross-ref: CMP.

LOG-012 · m · isolated — Approval or gate resolution accepted after hold_deadline until the next sweep

  • ddl/03-functions.sql:464-466 (checks starts_at only); sweep interval application.yaml:54. With ERR-001 the window can stretch to a whole relay pass.

LOG-013 · m · isolated — Ending a rule with an explicit date can extend an already-ended rule

  • sql/management/end_availability_rule.sql:3-9 has no guard; {effectiveUntil: 2099-01-01} revives a rule ended in the past.

Error handling (ERR) — 3/10 · 7 open

ERR-001 · C · isolated — A broker outage starves the hold-expiry and auto-complete sweeps: all three jobs share one scheduler thread

  • worker/WorkerSchedules.kt:20-21, 41-42, 47-48; application.yaml:7-9 (virtual threads → SimpleAsyncTaskScheduler; its fixed-delay executor has core size 1, per javap of spring-context 7.0.9); core/outbox/OutboxRelay.kt:28-50; worker/KafkaEventPublisher.kt:42-43
  • Worksheet: reach worker replicas during any broker outage with a backlog · residue external (HELD bookings stay HELD past hold_deadline, holding capacity; lapsed holds remain approvable) · signal none (no alerting) → critical
  • Evidence: 100 events × 10 s .get, or × 60 s max.block.ms (not overridden), gives one relay pass of roughly 17–100 min. Expiry runs only between passes. This contradicts the outbox_event design comment "a broker outage … never fails a booking". No TaskScheduler or pool is configured (worker/WorkerConfig.kt:27-57).
  • Cross-ref: CON, LOG-012.

ERR-002 · M · widespread — Caller mistakes become 500 "internal error" plus an ERROR "unhandled defect" stack trace

  • api/ApiExceptionHandler.kt:39-45 (catch-all, which wins over Spring's defaults). It catches:

- type mismatch on every UUID or Instant param - a missing @RequestParam, malformed JSON, or an unknown route - Page require (core/listing/Listing.kt:36-39) - DB CHECK or UNIQUE violations from caller input: timezone (ddl/01:94), blank names, dayOfWeek, endsAt ≤ startsAt (ddl/01:263), a duplicate linkedSubject (ddl/01:139)

  • Worksheet: reach any token holder · residue request · signal caller (wrong class, rule "none") → major; widespread: every controller module.
  • Evidence (probe): /v1/providers/not-a-uuid/availability → 500 {"code":"INTERNAL","rule":"none"}; POST /v1/providers {"timezone":"Mars/Olympus"} → 500 plus an ERROR log line. NF8 is lost.
  • Cross-ref: CMP (error shape), LGG (noise at ERROR).

ERR-003 · M · isolated — Provider creation is two autocommit statements

  • core/management/ProviderSetup.kt:61-66; repo/JdbcProviderSetupRepository.kt:25-44 (dropped .update() at :43); there is no @Transactional or TransactionTemplate anywhere in src
  • Worksheet: reach POST /v1/providers with a failure between the statements (connection drop, pod kill) · residue external (a provider with no admin, unmanageable; a retry creates a second provider) · signal caller (500) → major
  • Breaks the house rule "every multi-statement write is one function, one transaction" (data-design.md:424).
  • Cross-ref: PAT, SEC-002.

ERR-004 · m · isolated — Gate consumer commits the inbox dedupe claim before the effect (latent)

  • core/gate/GateResolutionService.kt:34-41, 80-83; repo/JdbcWorkerRepositories.kt:101-124; contradicts the inbox_message comment at ddl/01:~480 ("same transaction as the effect").
  • A redelivery after a failure is answered DUPLICATE, so the resolution is lost.
  • Latent: no producer exists (not exercised). If the edge becomes live, this is external + none → C.
  • Cross-ref: PAT, CON.

ERR-005 · m · isolated — Malformed gate resolution is retried, then skipped, with no dead-letter (owner declined hazard, domain-context §7)

  • worker/GateResolutionListener.kt:20-23 (the comment promises dead-lettering), :46-68; no CommonErrorHandler or DeadLetterPublishingRecoverer bean exists. Latent (no producer); external + none → C once live.

ERR-006 · m · isolated — A resolution for an unknown booking is answered with silence (latent; owner unknown §8)

  • core/gate/GateResolutionService.kt:44-45, 75.

ERR-007 · m · widespread — Setup and availability writes are not idempotent on retry

  • ProviderSetup.kt:61-80, AvailabilityManagement.kt:76-104, JdbcBookingLifecycle.kt:69-87
  • A retry after a lost response creates duplicate providers, resources, services, rules or exceptions.
  • A repeated reschedule emits a second BookingRescheduled.
  • The rule commits before conflictsFor, so a failed read loses the R20 list.

Security (SEC) — 2/10 · 8 open

SEC-001 · C · isolated — Internal contacts endpoint serves any booking's customer PII to any token holder (I5 violated)

  • api/InternalController.kt:27-29 → core/listing/ListingService.kt:45 → repo/JdbcListingRepository.kt:59-73 → sql/listing/booking_contacts.sql:4-12 (WHERE b.public_ref only); sys/SecurityConfig.kt:25-27 (only authenticated())
  • Worksheet: reach any issuer-token holder with a booking ref that is not theirs · residue external (name, email, phone and cancellation reason disclosed to the wrong principal) · signal none → critical
  • Evidence: path variable bookingRef → unscoped SELECT. Refs appear in INFO logs, events and provider listings, and are minted from a non-cryptographic PRNG (SEC-004). Amplifier: the returned customerRef feeds onBehalfOfCustomerRef for a self-made provider (SEC-002). "No legitimate caller" (not exercised) does not bound an untrusted caller.
  • Cross-ref: REQ (R18, NF5).

SEC-002 · C · isolated — POST /v1/providers has no authorization and makes the caller the first admin (owner declined, domain-context §7)

  • api/ProviderSetupController.kt:28-47 → core/management/ProviderSetup.kt:61-66 → sql/management/insert_provider.sql, insert_provider_admin.sql:3-5
  • Worksheet: reach any issuer-token holder · residue external (provider and provider_admin rows grant PROVIDER capacity: bypass R4 lead time, and book on behalf of any customer whose ref it holds via BookingService.kt:71-78 / unscoped customer/find_id_by_ref.sql) · signal none → critical
  • Cross-ref: ERR-003, REQ (UC1/PD1).

SEC-003 · M · widespread — Raw PostgreSQL error text, with PL/pgSQL frames and internal ids, returned to clients

  • sys/BookingSqlExceptionTranslator.kt:40; repo/RuleViolations.kt:17; api/BookingOutcomeResponder.kt:83; RAISE texts with bigint ids at ddl/03-functions.sql:250, 423, 429, 560
  • Evidence (probe): BK001 detail = "ERROR: the resource is occupied … Where: PL/pgSQL function fn_create_booking(bigint,…) line 53 at RAISE". BK008 also acts as a cross-provider existence oracle for resource refs (find_resource_id.sql is unscoped). Weakened defense → major; widespread: every BK rejection on every write path.
  • Cross-ref: CMP, ERR.

SEC-004 · M · widespread — Public refs drawn from a non-cryptographic PRNG

  • sys/TimeAndIdConfig.kt:21 (RandomGenerator.getDefault(), L32X64MixRandom on JDK 25); sys/IdGenerator.kt:28-31
  • Evidence: every public_ref and event_id takes its random bits from it. Refs are the only barrier on SEC-001 and on "answer as absent", and architecture-design.md:313 calls them non-enumerable. Predictable tokens → major; widespread: every entity's ref.
  • Cross-ref: CON-005.

SEC-005 · M · isolated — Any token from the issuer is accepted; no audience restriction

Concurrency safety (CON) — 3/10 · 7 open

CON-001 · C · isolated — An availability edit racing a create stores a booking inside blocked time and omits it from the R20 conflict list

  • Worksheet: reach provider adds a BLOCK or ends a rule while a create for that window is in flight · residue external (corrected: a CONFIRMED booking is stored inside time already blocked when it committed, an outcome no serial order produces; verifier probe) · signal none → critical
  • Evidence (probe): with the create uncommitted, the BLOCK committed and the conflicts query returned 0. The create then committed CONFIRMED, and the same query returned 1.
  • Cross-ref: REQ (R20).

CON-002 · M · isolated — Concurrent creates of the same new group session fail with BK001 or deadlock instead of joining

Contract & compatibility (CMP) — 5/10 · 3 open

CMP-001 · M · isolated — No documented working path delivers a schema change to a database already at V1..V4

  • build.gradle.kts:64-80 copies only root ddl/*.sql and renames four fixed files. Related: README.md:96-99 (the DDL is the "single source of truth"), data-design.md:607 ("numbered directories"), application.yaml:16-18 (Flyway at every pod startup), and src/test/.../TestDatabase.kt:41-45 (always clean(); migrate()).
  • Mechanism answer: Flyway at startup from generated V1–V4. The routes a maintainer could follow:

- Editing in place, per README, changes the checksum, so validateOnMigrate fails at every pod startup. - A numbered directory, per data-design, is never copied. - A new 05-x.sql is copied without the V prefix and silently ignored. - Only an undocumented hand-named V5__x.sql works.

  • Worksheet: reach the first schema change after deployment · residue process (all pods fail at startup, on the README route) · signal operator (startup crash) → major. The data-design and new-file routes leave the change unapplied with no signal (external + none). The verifier confirmed the documents disagree, so the tier is read from the README route.

Credited as intentional (recorded to prevent re-litigation)

  • Outbox at-least-once delivery: an unlocked claim, a republish after a lost ack or a timed-out send, and duplicates across relays. Evidence: claim_due_events.sql:6-10 and domain-context §7 ("consumers must dedupe on eventId"). This covers duplicates only, not reordering (LOG-003).
  • The outbox never drops an event: the row is retained, the error recorded, and backoff capped at 5 min (OutboxRelay.kt:9-12, domain-context §7). Escalation is a separate matter (REQ-002).
  • The Idempotency-Key is optional, so a keyless retry creates a new booking (ddl/01-create-tables.sql:394, R15). REQ-015 records the deviation from the design document only.
  • The customer profile commits before the booking; provisioning on first use is idempotent (BookingPorts.kt:46-61, upsert_customer.sql:1-4).
  • Both sweeps run on every replica, with SKIP LOCKED and re-evaluation under lock (Sweeps.kt:7-9, ddl/03:640-648, domain-context §4). This does not cover the deadlock exposure (CON-003).
  • Lookup ids are stable and never renumbered (04-seed-lookups.sql:1-2); RDB-001 is kept for readability only.
  • Client contact details fill only the gaps the token leaves (domain-context §5, owner-confirmed).
